observer: Codex (GPT-6, desktop harness), one visual reader; no independent source review claimed
scope: Targeted examples and a four-object source-table sample, not a random estimate of transcription accuracy

sources: CISI 1 printed166/PDF202, H-9 A and impression a
observations.observation: Two groups of four and three short strokes stand beside the plain fish shape. The object view and impression reverse their displayed order.
observations.decision: Supports the graphic seven-plus-fish example; neither view specifies a constellation independently.

sources: CISI 2 printed339/PDF374, H-912 B and B bis
observations.observation: Figure 6 matches H-912 B's fish-like sign, open V-shaped sign and four strokes, including the surrounding tablet outline. The 2010 figure caption and prose call the object H-902, while citing CISI 2 page339.
observations.decision: Link this version of Figure 6 to H-912 B. Preserve the published H-902 label as a conflicting bibliographic assertion.

sources: Local files H-902_A.jpg and H-502_B.jpg, the latter correctly indexed by its printed H-902 B caption
observations.observation: These photographs show different oval or enclosed signs and do not match Figure 6. The pinned transcription has no B220-family fish on either face.
observations.decision: Keep H-902 as a separate control object. The older file-name error and the paper's H-902/H-912 reference error are separate issues.

observations.observation: The tablet has a V-shaped sign with four strokes and a scene of a person extending an angular object toward a tree. No B220-family sign occurs in the pinned text.
observations.decision: Retain as the pictorial comparison used for a vessel reading. Its exclusion from the fish-bearing denominator is correct.

observations.observation: Face A shows a long-snouted animal with an elongated fish-like figure at its mouth and a separate fish-shaped sign at the right. Other faces show different animal imagery. The scan does not identify the inscribed word's pronunciation.
observations.decision: Supports the pictorial fish comparison; the multiple faces are one physical object.

observations.observation: The caption and fish-family glyph on the seal are visible. The image does not itself verify the published room or depth.
observations.decision: Photo identity and catalogue context are separate assertions.

observations.observation: The photograph clearly shows a plain fish form beside two long strokes; one edge is broken.
observations.decision: Retain the long-stroke class separately from short numeral groups.

observations.observation: The long rectangular seal shows two fish-family forms among other signs. Caption identity is clear.
observations.decision: The sample includes a rectangular carrier rather than only square animal seals.

observations.observation: A fish-family form and other signs are visible above an elephant. Some fine components are blurred.
observations.decision: The plate supports family-level presence, not every fine-code distinction.

observations.observation: Adjacent fish-family forms are visible in a photograph selected because its transcription reverses one relation in the learned order.
observations.decision: Keep the counterexample; a source specialist should adjudicate fine variants and direction before changing the corpus.

observations.observation: Two short strokes appear between an opening sign and the following fish-shaped form. This is a direct visual example of a value outside 3, 6 and 7 under the tally interpretation.
observations.decision: The strokes could have a connective function. Do not equate this observation with a secure astronomical numeral counterexample.

observations.observation: No photograph was linked in the held image index. The transcription-only outside-set case remains unverified by a plate.
observations.decision: Keep the missing-image case in the selection log; seek the later CISI photograph.

observations.observation: The selected reversal has no resolved CISI identifier or linked image.
observations.decision: Retain its uncertainty and do not treat it as a new archaeological observation.

independence: The papers and local crops often reproduce the same CISI photograph. They verify attribution or interpretation history, not additional physical specimens.
